title: Hybrid role handoff activation stencil — 30d
summary: Lightweight 30-day activation stencil for hybrid hires that combines a 72-hour mentor sprint with role handoff checkpoints, hardware/access orchestration, interview evidence transfer, and success signals for managers and mentors.
content:
Purpose:
This stencil is designed for hybrid-role hires (part-remote, part-onsite) where quick productive ramp and continuity of work are critical. It focuses on a first 72-hour mentor sprint to transfer tacit knowledge, followed by a 30-day activation plan and clear success signals for the new hire, mentor, and hiring manager.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to individual contributor and IC-to-manager transitions across engineering, product, and platform teams.
- Assumes standard RW access provisioning pipeline (Okta, GCP, GitHub, internal Slack).
- Intended to be used by hiring managers, onboarding coordinators, and mentors.
- Lightweight: can be completed without large cross-functional coordination; escalate if blocked >48 hours.

Quick overview (how teams use this):
1) Pre-boarding (before day 0): hiring manager completes the Role Activation Card and shares with mentor and devops.
2) Day 0–3: 72-hour mentor sprint — hands-on shadowing, small verify tasks, access validation, micro-architecture walkthroughs.
3) Day 4–30: 30-day activation cadence — progressive responsibilities, one canary deliverable, weekly check-ins and pulse survey.
4) Triage and escalation: issues tracked in JIRA-HANDOFF-88; People Ops notified on day 3 if blockers remain.

Pre-boarding checklist (owner: hiring manager) — complete 5 business days before start:
- Confirm job-specific Role Activation Card: team objectives, top 3 deliverables in first 30 days, required repos/services, and immediate peers.
- Assign mentor (ideally cross-team pair): share mentor charter and 72-hour plan.
- Submit hardware request (laptop + peripherals) with preferred shipping schedule; confirm onsite desk booking if hybrid onsite days required.
- Provision access tickets: Okta groups, GitHub teams, GCP project permission template (apply least privilege).
- Share 1-pager with new hire: Day-0 agenda, Slack channels, people to ping for quick help.

72-hour mentor sprint (owner: mentor) — objective: remove first-day friction and transfer 80% of tacit onboarding knowledge:
Day 0 (welcome + access validation):
- 09:00: Quick intro call (manager + mentor) — expectations and 72-hour sprint goals (20m).
- 09:30: Access validation checklist — confirm SSH, GitHub, CI pipeline access, email, calendar, Slack, VPN (if required).
- 10:30: Tour of codebase and routing: README-to-repo map, important services, test harnesses (30–45m).
- Afternoon: small sandbox task (run tests, make a tiny docs change) with pair session for support.

Day 1 (deep dive + shadowing):
- Morning: architecture walkthrough of primary service(s) — ask the 5 why’s, highlight known incidents and hot paths.
- Midday: pair on a real but low-risk issue; mentor demonstrates the debug flow end-to-end.
- Late afternoon: access to monitoring and dashboards; show alerting baseline.

Day 2 (ownership & canary work):
- Assign a micro-deliverable that touches the codepath and CI (e.g., add a metric, update a small config, fix a docs bug).
- Shadow mentor through code review and merge process; practice release steps in a sandbox environment.
- End-of-day: 30-minute retro with manager to confirm remaining knowledge gaps.

72-hour deliverables (evidence to record in JIRA):
- Sandbox PR merged to a non-production branch (or a docs update).
- Access validation sheet completed and signed-off.
- Mentor notes artifact: top 5 gotchas and recommended learning next steps.

30-day activation plan (owner: manager) — weekly cadence:
Week 1 (days 4–7): Stabilize and short wins
- Focus: complete on-call readout (if applicable), finish onboarding tickets, attend product syncs.
- Deliverable: complete the canary task and get feedback on code quality and review etiquette.
- Checkpoint: 1:1 with manager at end of week to surface blockers.

Week 2: Expand scope and cross-team orientation
- Focus: begin ownership of a small feature or infra task; meet cross-functional collaborators.
- Deliverable: draft design doc or implementation plan for the first feature.
- Checkpoint: mentor-led coding session; People Ops pulse (short form).

Week 3: Independent contribution + feedback loop
- Focus: complete the first feature’s implementation and ship to staging.
- Deliverable: merge to mainline or schedule for deployment window.
- Checkpoint: manager 1:1 and peer feedback summary.

Week 4: Impact and next-month plan
- Focus: handoff minor tasks, document known gaps, set next 60-day objectives.
- Deliverable: 30-day reflection note from the hire (what went well, what didn’t, top 3 learning topics).
- Checkpoint: formal 30-day review meeting (manager + mentor + people ops optional).

Role handoff artifacts (what mentor hands over):
- Short ‘how-to’ README for daily ops (start/stop, common debug commands, typical incident triage steps).
- List of 8 critical Slack threads and owners.
- One prioritized incident postmortem to study.
- Mini architecture map (one page) that highlights service boundaries and data flows.

Interview evidence transfer guidance (for those transitioning from candidate to hire):
- Embed candidate exercise notes (what they shipped in the takehome) in the Role Activation Card.
- If candidate had a design interview, attach that design doc and the interviewer rubric summary.
- Use the interview rubrics (engineer-core, infra, product) to seed initial 30-day goals where applicable.

Access & hardware orchestration (practical notes):
- If hardware delivery will be delayed >48 hrs, prepare a temporary loaner and remote VPN onboarding call.
- Onsite days: ensure desk/Badge + visitor access are coordinated in advance and included on Day-0 agenda.
- Key credentials: never email secrets; use KMS or secrets manager references in Role Activation Card.

Success signals (how we measure healthy activation):
- Green: new hire completes 72-hour deliverables, merges a sandbox PR, passes access checks, and is contributing code/reviews by week 2.
- Yellow: access inconsistency or 72-hour blocker; daily check-ins with People Ops until resolved.
- Red: after 10 business days, still unable to complete sandbox deliverable or persistent missing permissions — escalate to People Ops + Manager + IT lead.

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: missing context for recurring alerts. Mitigation: mentor runs a one-hour incident walkthrough and provides annotated runbook.
- Failure: hardware late. Mitigation: loaner + prioritized remote tasks that do not require local GPUs.
- Failure: unclear expectations. Mitigation: manager publishes a 30-day success rubric with objective examples.

Template messages (short snippets):
- To mentor: “Thanks for taking this on — primary goal: remove first-week friction and get X to merge a sandbox PR. Please document top 5 gotchas in the mentor notes.”
- To new hire Day-0: “Welcome! Here’s your Day-0 schedule, access checklist, and the Slack channels to join. Ping me if anything is blocked.”

Appendix — mentor charter (short):
- Time commitment: ~6–8 hours during first 72 hours, then 1hr/wk for 4 weeks.
- Goals: get hire to a safe productive baseline, produce artifacts listed above, and identify long-term growth areas.
- If mentor cannot complete responsibilities, escalate to manager within 24 hours.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Suggested pulse at day 7 and day 21 to collect asynchronous written feedback (quick form).
- Capture mentor notes in the team’s onboarding folder and link to the Role Activation Card.
- This stencil is intentionally lightweight; adapt for senior hires by extending the 72-hour sprint to include cross-team design reviews.

End of document.
